name: Kuwait
headline: Kuwait: +2.7% growth in 2025, 2.4% inflation, debt 15% of GDP
sections: Kuwait is a $157 billion economy (2025), the world's 60th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.7% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $56K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 7.7% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 2.4% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 4.0% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 2.2% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 15.1% (2025).
Gross government debt is 15% of GDP (2025), a low level that has risen from 10% in 2020. The general government balance is +24.5% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +22.7% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 94% of GDP (2024), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 38% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 84.6 years (2024). Population: 5.0 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
